title: Abba (tanna during the Temple period)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Peah ch. 2, mishnah 6: an incident in which Rabbi Shimon of Mitzpeh sowed [a field] and [came] before Rabban Gamliel [the Elder], and they went up to the Chamber of Hewn Stone and inquired. Nahum the Scribe said: I have a tradition from Rabbi Miyasha, who received it from Abba, who received it from the Pairs (zugot). According to Hyman’s chronology, this Abba was a disciple of Hillel and Shammai, who were the last of the Pairs; so Rashi and Tosafot explained in Nazir 56b. But some read that he received it "from his father," and so it is in the commentary of the Rosh on Nazir 56b. And in Yuchasin, first essay, entry R' Yishmael, he cites from the Tosefta, Beitzah ch. 3, the following: "They said of R' Abba, and of Rabbi Eleazar son of R' Tzadok, and of Abba Shaul ben Batnit, that they were shopkeepers in Jerusalem." If we uphold his reading (for in our Tosefta the words 'R' Abba' are absent), he is this Abba mentioned in Peah, as we explained in the entry R' Eleazar bar Tzadok, that he was the father of R' Tzadok who lived at the time of the Destruction, and this R' Eleazar was in the time of R' Gamliel the Elder.

notes.text: The readings “from Abba” and “from his father” are distinct. Hyman’s Tosefta quotation comes through Yuchasin; he reports that Rabbi Abba is absent in his Tosefta. The compressed closing father/son antecedent still needs clarification.

Two whole saved digital scalars were read with raw SHA256, exact selectors, scalar hashes and actual edition metadata checked: Torat Emet357 Mishnah Peah2:6 (425 chars) and Machon Mamre Tosefta Beitzah3 selected text[5] (621 chars). The Mishnah explicitly gives Rabbi Shimon of Mitzpeh, Rabban Gamliel, and Rabbi Miyasha locally; it has from Abba, distinct from Hyman's reported Rosh reading from his father. Hyman's bracketed [came] and [the Elder] remain brackets and are not supplied as words in that Mishnah scalar. The Pairs received chain, first-person I have a tradition, plural went up and inquired, Hillel and Shammai as the final Pairs, and Hyman's attributed chronological conclusion retain their force; no new genealogy or chronology is admitted. The separate Yuchasin entry Yishmael title, quoted Abba title, father Tzadok title, later Elazar cross-reference and repeated Elazar title, and final contextual Gamliel abbreviation remain R' without transferring the initial full Rabban or locally supported Tosefta Rabbi. The selected Tosefta quote explicitly gives Rabbi Elazar bar untitled Tzadok and untitled Abba Shaul ben Batnit as shopkeepers in Jerusalem; it lacks Abba in that selected quoted list, without proving absence throughout the work or across editions. Rabbi before Elazar in the quoted clause is locally supported; Tzadok remains R' in the supplied quotation because Hyman separately abbreviates his title there. Hyman's Yuchasin-mediated quotation including R' Abba, his parenthesis about our Tosefta, and the conditional if we uphold his reading remain distinct from the named digital Tosefta. Neither Yuchasin, Rashi, Tosafot nor Rosh Nazir56b is newly checked here. The later father/son antecedent and cross-referenced Elazar bar Tzadok argument remain unresolved; the prior search's local-heading nonmatch is historical, not global absence. No additional Mishnah transmission through prophets, Sinai or agricultural law, nor the Tosefta measures or later legal continuation, is imported. All two original mixed notes, the current mixed note, all old English and carried material remain exact; no requested mixed-note revision is applied. The original spacing-as-digitization-artifact interpretation stays historical and is not new printed-pixel or correction-history proof. This additive qualification retains source hold p001.

The printed notice (volume I, p. 1) and Mishnah Peah 2:6 retain “from Abba”; “from his father” remains Hyman’s separate report of the Rosh. Tosafot on Nazir 56b explicitly identifies the Pairs as Hillel and Shammai. The selected Tosefta Beitzah 3 list names Elazar bar Tzadok and Abba Shaul ben Batnit but lacks Abba in that list; this does not establish the reading of Yuchasin or every Tosefta edition. Hyman’s cross-referenced discussion of Elazar bar Tzadok (volume I, pp. 201–202) proposes an earlier Elazar as the father of the Tzadok associated with the Destruction, distinguishing him from the later Elazar son of Tzadok. He uses the shopkeepers’ notice and Abba Shaul’s chronology in constructing that account. This clarifies the closing father/son antecedent as Hyman’s reconstruction, without independently establishing the genealogy. The identification with the Abba in Peah remains conditional on upholding the Yuchasin reading. The exact Yuchasin and Rosh passages have not been independently collated.
